title: Osmosis across a partially permeable membrane
caption: Water molecules cross the membrane both ways, but more cross from the dilute solution, so the net movement of water is into the concentrated solution. The sugar molecules are too big to cross.
alt: Two solutions separated by a partially permeable membrane. The dilute solution on the left has many water molecules and few sugar molecules; the concentrated solution on the right has fewer water molecules and more sugar molecules. Small arrows show water crossing both ways, three to the right and one to the left, and a large arrow shows the net movement of water to the right.
description: Left: a dilute solution, mostly water molecules with two sugar molecules.
Right: a concentrated solution, with fewer water molecules and seven sugar molecules.
Water molecules pass through the membrane's pores in both directions; more pass from left to right.
The sugar molecules are bigger than the pores and stay on their side.
Net movement of water: from the dilute solution into the concentrated solution.
